messages:
Marcus Lee: Heads-up — CobaltPay wants a short POC to validate a drop-in compat shim for their existing competitor API. Questions from presales: pricing delta for proxying, security questionnaire, and how we handle prompt/response parity. Can SEs + security chime in?

Priya Patel: I can drive the technical POC. Quick checklist request: (1) customer test prompts + failure cases, (2) expected latency SLOs, (3) acceptance criteria for output parity (examples).

Tess Nguyen: @Priya +1. Also need to confirm whether they want token-for-token billing parity or an SLA-backed fixed throughput. Pricing changes if we route through an adapter (extra compute).

Marcus Lee: They asked for two things: token parity (so their billing system doesn't break) and a predictable per-call latency budget (<= 250ms tail for short chats). They also flagged legal: KMS integration and SOC2 evidence.

Priya Patel: For parity — biggest gotchas are tokenization differences (our tokenizer vs theirs), stop-sequence behavior, and deterministic sampling seeds. We'll need to run prompt equivalence tests. I can prepare a small harness. Example proxy mapping curl for them to test quickly:

```bash
# hitting our compat proxy that maps competitor args -> Redwood API
curl -X POST https://compat.cobalt.cobaltpay.example/api/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <COBALT_TEST_KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"Summarize invoice #123","max_tokens":64,"temperature":0.0}'
```

Priya Patel: The shim will translate max_tokens -> max_new_tokens, model names, and emulate their stop token semantics. We'll log token counts so their billing can verify.

Jordan Kim: Networking note: for CobaltPay's staging, we'll need their allowlist IPs if they want fixed egress. If they run in their VPC we can provide connector docs. Also: if we enable auditing for the POC, be aware extra retention may be billable.

Olivia Sanchez: Security Qs: send over the customer security questionnaire (they attached a 10-page doc). We need to answer: data residency, retention, KMS/HSM key control, tenant isolation, vulnerability management, pen-test results, and export controls. I'll take lead on responses — please drop any technical artifacts here.

Marcus Lee: Dropping the questionnaire link: https://cobaltpay.example/secq/cobalt-llm-poc.pdf. They flagged an enterprise blocker: "no third-party tokens stored in cleartext" and a request for a brief SAML SSO demo.

Priya Patel: For token handling we can support transient token forwarding + optional token masking. We do not persist raw customer API keys by default in hosted mode; we can show flow:

```text
client -> proxy (transient) -> Redwood runtime (KV cache)
logs: redacted keys, token counts only
```

Tess Nguyen: Pricing impact: if they want token-level billing parity, we'll provide an adapter surcharge estimate. Rough numbers: hosted passthrough adds ~5-10% compute depending on avg tokens; dedicated reserved pool can be flat monthly with predictable unit cost. I'll prepare numbers in an email.

Marcus Lee: Timeline ask from the customer: 2-week POC, with first 3 days for sandbox setup, then 7 days of smoke tests, final 4 days for parity tuning and sign-off. Is that realistic?

Priya Patel: Yes. Proposed milestone checklist:
- Day 0-3: sandbox credentials + allowlist 
- Day 4-10: run canonical prompt suite (we need their 50 prompts)
- Day 11-13: tuning (stop tokens, det-sampling), stability tests
- Day 14: acceptance meeting + artifact deliverables (logs, latency/throughput report, parity diff report)

Priya Patel: Acceptance criteria (example):
- median latency <= 120ms, p95 <= 250ms for short prompts
- <2% response drift on curated prompt set (semantic equivalence as judged by their eval set)
- no persisted customer keys in plaintext

Jordan Kim: For the parity diffs we can produce a CSV: prompt, cobalt_response, redwood_response, token_delta, notes. We'll run an automatic similarity score (BLEU/embedding-sim) and mark high-delta items for manual review.

Olivia Sanchez: Also add: requirement to provide SOC2 Type II date & pen-test report. We can supply SOC2 summary + contact for security review. If they require HSM-backed keys, mention we have KMS integrations with external key wraps (KMIP/HSM via private).

Tess Nguyen: One question for product: will we honor their custom header like X-Cust-Request-Id and echo it back? Some of their infra relies on it for tracing.

Priya Patel: Yes we can map and echo custom headers through the proxy; we'll add a passthrough list in the mapping config. Example mapping snippet: 

```json
{
  "passthrough_headers": ["X-Cust-Request-Id","X-Trace-Id"],
  "token_translation": "max_tokens->max_new_tokens",
  "stop_behavior": "honor-first-stop"
}
```

Marcus Lee: Legal asked about indemnity and export controls — flagged as potential blocker. I've looped in legal; will update. For the POC we might need an NDA amendment.

Priya Patel: Can CobaltPay share a small set of failing prompts they currently see on competitor? If they send 10 'problem' prompts I can prioritize parity fixes.

Marcus Lee: They said they'll attach the prompts to the security questionnaire email.

Olivia Sanchez: I'll start drafting answers to the secQ, will call out any infra changes that would increase compliance overhead. If they want on-prem deployment, that's a different engagement (Private) and pricing.

Jordan Kim: Ops note: enable verbose logging during POC but route logs to a customer-visible bucket for them to verify token counts; we can set a 7-day retention. Will need to document retention in the secQ answer.

Tess Nguyen: I'll prepare a short pricing matrix: hosted-adapter surcharge, dedicated reserved estimate, and private deployment rough range. Will share EOD.

Marcus Lee: Ok — action items: Priya to send proxy curl + test harness, Tess to send preliminary pricing, Olivia to start secQ answers, Jordan to prepare ops instructions for allowlist & logs. Target: sandbox ready in 48-72 hours.

Priya Patel: Starting on harness now. I'll push the repo link here when ready.

redwood-deploy-bot: New sandbox created for customer 'cobaltpay-staging-001' (ids: sbx-77). Credentials: will be posted to secure vault.

Marcus Lee: Perfect, thanks all. We'll sync with CobaltPay tomorrow @ 10am PT. :thumbsup:
